task.name: Simplify model config with first-class transport
task.story_text:
## Summary

Model configuration should have one clean normalized shape. Transport must be a first-class field, not encoded in provider-like prefixes (`openai-api/`, `gemini-cli/`) or inferred from legacy sibling fields (`cli` plus `provider`).

This does not need to preserve the existing `forge.yaml` contract. A breaking config cleanup is acceptable if it removes the old leakage and leaves one model abstraction that is easy to reason about.

Today, the same model name can mean different execution paths depending on where it appears: a built-in registry key, a custom overlay provider token, or a provider fallback. Local OpenAI-compatible models add another wrinkle: locality is endpoint metadata (`base_url`), not a transport kind.

## Desired behavior

A selected model has one normalized identity:

- provider family, for example `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, or `deepseek`
- provider model name, for example `gpt-5.4`, `sonnet`, or `qwen2.5-coder:32b`
- transport kind, with bounded values `cli` or `api`

That tuple is the canonical identity. Do not add a separate free-form model `id` that can drift from the provider/model/transport tuple. If a friendly display label is needed, it must not be the lookup key.

Execution details are derived from identity where unambiguous:

- `(openai, cli)` resolves to the Codex CLI runner
- `(anthropic, cli)` resolves to the Claude CLI runner
- `(google, cli)` resolves to the Gemini CLI runner
- `(openai, api)` resolves to the OpenAI API adapter
- `(google, api)` resolves to the Google API adapter
- `(deepseek, api)` resolves to the DeepSeek API adapter

Only require an explicit runner/executor when there are genuinely multiple valid runners for the same provider and transport kind.

Routing policy is separate from model identity. Tier, capability, cost rank, dev capability, and phase eligibility may still be configured or derived, but they should live in an explicit routing/policy layer rather than being confused with the identity of the model itself. Pricing metadata is similarly metadata used for accounting, not part of the model identity.

Local LLMs are API transports with endpoint metadata:

- `transport.kind: api`
- `provider: openai` or another OpenAI-compatible adapter family
- `base_url` pointing at a localhost-ish endpoint such as `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, or `0.0.0.0`

Do not introduce a `local/...` provider prefix or a `local` transport kind. Locality is endpoint metadata.

The loader may choose to reject old spellings instead of supporting aliases. If temporary aliases are kept for operator convenience, they must terminate at the raw input boundary. After loading, no legacy transport state should remain: no fake provider prefixes, no duplicated `cli`/`provider` dispatch inference, and no fallback shape that has to be interpreted differently from normal model transport.

## Example

```yaml
models:
  enabled:
    - provider: openai
      model: gpt-5.5
      transport:
        kind: cli
      routing:
        tier: strong

    - provider: openai
      model: gpt-5.5
      transport:
        kind: api
      routing:
        tier: strong

    - provider: openai
      model: qwen2.5-coder:32b
      transport:
        kind: api
      base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1
      routing:
        tier: fast
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. The model config schema has a first-class transport object with a bounded `kind` enum of `cli` and `api`.
2. Canonical model identity is derived from provider, model, and transport kind. There is no required free-form `id` that can diverge from that tuple.
3. CLI/API selection is never encoded in provider-like prefixes in normalized config. Existing keys such as `openai-api/...` or `gemini-cli/...` are removed or treated only as raw input aliases.
4. Runner/executor is inferred from provider plus transport kind where unambiguous; config only requires an explicit runner when the tuple has more than one valid executor.
5. Local LLMs are represented as API transports with endpoint metadata such as `base_url`; local is not a separate provider prefix or transport kind.
6. Routing policy is separate from identity. Tier, capability, cost rank, dev capability, and phase eligibility do not define the model identity.
7. Provider/model identity and transport identity are preserved distinctly in status, audit, model profile, and assignment telemetry.
8. Provider fallback configuration is renamed or normalized so it is clearly a transport fallback from CLI to API, not a provider-family fallback.
9. After loading, runtime dispatch reads only the normalized transport object. It does not infer dispatch from legacy `cli`/`provider` field combinations.
10. Legacy transport fields and names are removed from runtime-facing dataclasses where practical; any retained compatibility fields are confined to raw parsing/migration code and are not the source of dispatch truth.
11. Documentation shows only the canonical shape as the recommended configuration. Any old shape, if documented, is marked as rejected or migration-only.

## Relationship to existing work

This supersedes the narrow transport portion of #751. That issue can either be closed as covered by this broader cleanup or kept only for its unrelated config-type cleanup items (`PlanConfig.validate_spec`, `RetryPolicy.plan_escalation_threshold`, and `NotificationConfig.human_review_timeout_seconds` loader/default drift).

handoff.summary: Normalized model configuration around a canonical (provider, model, transport.kind) identity. AGENT_REGISTRY is re-keyed to <provider>/<model>/<cli|api>; the openai-api/ and gemini-cli/ prefixes survive only as raw-input aliases normalized at the lookup/parse boundary (normalize_model_key, resolve_agent_spec, ForgeConfig.__post_init__). Runner/executor is derived from (provider, kind) by transport_for(), with an explicit runner required only for the genuinely ambiguous gh-aw tuple. Routing knobs moved into a RoutingPolicy container on AgentSpec so they cannot be confused with identity; pricing and base_url are metadata. Local OpenAI-compatible models are now API transports carrying a localhost base_url, which flows registry -> ModelInfo -> ModelRef/AgentDef -> ModelProfile. models.enabled accepts the canonical mapping form ({provider, model, transport:{kind}, routing, base_url, cost}) alongside identity strings, and models.custom declarations are re-keyed to their identity with the declaration name kept only as a parse-time alias. ModelProfile/PlanConfig/ModelRef share one _normalize_transport() that turns the raw cli/provider spelling into a TransportSpec once at construction and then mirrors cli from it, so the two cannot diverge; dispatch (runners/cli.py), auth, and both fallback builders read transport only. ApiFallbackConfig became TransportFallbackConfig with a transport() accessor, provider_fallbacks became transport_fallback (old key rejected with a message naming the new one), auto_api_fallback became auto_transport_fallback. Telemetry surfaces emit provider, model and transport kind distinctly via provider_family/transport_kind/identity_label. Docs, forge.yaml and the generated default config show only the canonical shape.

handoff.summary: Iteration 1 fixes the transport-only override defect and the non-canonical docs. The three code P1s were one bug at two call sites: _resolve_override_transport / _resolve_ref_override_transport computed the correct TransportSpec for an `overrides.<role>.transport: {kind: ...}` block, but the caller then constructed ModelProfile/ModelRef with the cli inherited from the profile being overridden; _normalize_transport's cli-wins-on-conflict rule re-derived the old transport from that stale cli, so the switch silently no-opped unless the operator also changed provider/cli. Added models.mirror_fields_for_transport(transport, cli, provider), which returns the (cli, provider) pair mirroring a resolved transport (CLI -> (runner, None), API -> (None, provider_family), unresolvable -> pair untouched so bad values still surface in errors), and applied it in both _apply_profile_overrides and _apply_ref_overrides immediately after the transport is resolved. Verified cli->api and api->cli at the ModelProfile level, the ModelRef level, the loader level (dev and review_pool), and through derive_roles -> bridge -> ModelProfile. Audited the other seven runtime sites that pair cli/provider with a transport (auto-assign, agent pool, bridge, apply_model_info swaps, _build_api_fallback_profile, _build_cli_fallback_api_profile, _apply_transport_fallback, assignment._agent_to_profile) — all already self-consistent. For the docs P1, rewrote all five recommended patterns in choose-your-provider-setup.md and the primary example in local-models.md into the canonical models:/transport shape (local models as api transports with base_url and zero per-token cost), and marked the classic profiles: block in inputs-reference.md explicitly LEGACY. Every YAML example in those guides was run through load_config to confirm it loads and yields the documented role assignments.

reviews.summary: [openai-gpt-5.5] The model registry and loader mostly implement the canonical transport shape, but explicit transport overrides can still be overwritten by inherited legacy cli state, and one guide still recommends a non-canonical local profile shape. | [google-gemini-3.5-flash] Approved: Normalized model configuration around a canonical (provider, model, transport.kind) identity with first-class transport. | [claude-sonnet] Canonical transport identity is well-built end to end, but the profile/ref override path silently no-ops a transport-kind switch when it isn't paired with a provider/cli key change, contradicting AC1/AC9 and the code's own stated guarantee.

findings.description: A models config with overrides.dev.transport.kind set to api on a CLI-derived dev profile loads the dev profile as the Codex CLI transport instead of the OpenAI API transport.
The local/privacy-first provider setup guide presents the recommended configuration as profiles entries with provider: openai and no first-class transport object.

Applying an override of the canonical form overrides.dev.transport: {kind: api} to a CLI-transport profile (e.g. cli=claude) leaves the resulting ModelProfile's transport, mode, and cli fields unchanged at cli/'cli' instead of switching to the API transport, even though _resolve_override_transport correctly computed the API TransportSpec.

The same defect exists in _apply_ref_overrides: overriding a ModelRef with {'transport': {'kind': 'api'}} alone (no 'cli'/'provider' keys) computes the correct API TransportSpec in _resolve_ref_override_transport, but the constructed ModelRef still carries the old cli value, and ModelRef.__post_init__ re-derives the transport from that stale cli, discarding the intended switch.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1] [claude-opus] The loader and profile-builder modules that own the raw-input boundary are absent from every step: src/theforge/config/load.py and src/theforge/config/profiles.py. This is not a stylistic omission — profiles.py:212-282 (_apply_profile_overrides, and _apply_ref_overrides alongside it) constructs ModelProfile with transport=None on purpose, with a docstring stating it relies on __post_init__ re-inferring TransportSpec from the effective cli/provider pair. Step 3 deletes exactly that inference, so every forge.yaml profile override would produce a profile with no transport, and dispatch at runners/cli.py:440-449 falls through to profile.cli (which the same step removes). Likewise load.py:251 calls overlay_transport(provider) from models.py — the function Step 2 rewrites — and load.py:400/1033-1124 still builds profiles from cli=/provider= pairs.
  Suggestion: Add src/theforge/config/load.py and src/theforge/config/profiles.py to Steps 2, 3, and 4, and state the replacement contract explicitly: profiles.py override/ref-override paths must construct the TransportSpec directly (from the effective provider + transport.kind) instead of passing transport=None, and load.py must normalize provider-prefix aliases and cli/provider raw keys into transport at parse time so nothing downstream re-infers. Check src/theforge/config/_loaders.py for the same pattern while there.
- [P1] [claude-opus] Step 4 (fallback rename) and Step 5 (telemetry) under-enumerate their callers. ApiFallbackConfig is constructed in load.py:299-326 (_derive_api_fallbacks, plus _validate_auto_api_fallback_schema and the auto_api_fallback raw key at load.py:330/759/765/904) and profiles.py:519-592, and consumed in runners/cli.py:222-384, sprint/runner.py:1384-1439, and assignment.py:1590. Identity/transport display consumers also include cli/check_config.py:197-275 (_split_provider_transport, _transport_label, _plan_transport_label, which read profile.cli/plan.cli directly) and src/theforge/model_profiles.py. None of these files or their directories appear in the plan, so renaming the fallback type or dropping ModelProfile.cli breaks them at import/attribute time.
  Suggestion: Extend Step 4's file list with config/load.py, config/profiles.py, runners/cli.py, sprint/runner.py, and assignment.py, and Step 5's with cli/check_config.py, model_profiles.py, assignment.py, and sprint/runner.py. Name concrete files rather than directories (src/theforge/coordinator, src/theforge/task) so coverage is checkable.
- [P1-impl] [claude-opus] PlanConfig (schema.py:54-65) carries its own cli/provider/api_fallback trio and calls infer_transport independently of ModelProfile; load.py:1049-1124 validates plan_cfg.cli against SUPPORTED_CLIS. The plan touches schema.py but never says whether PlanConfig converges on the same normalized transport shape.
  Suggestion: Dev should give PlanConfig the same transport object and drop the SUPPORTED_CLIS check, or explicitly note it as a raw-input-only field.
- [P2] [claude-opus] Step 7 lists three test files plus a bare tests entry, but the change touches sprint/runner.py, assignment.py, and cli/check_config.py, whose tests (e.g. tests/test_agent_spec.py, tests/test_config_schema.py, tests/test_empty_model_registry.py, which already import resolve_agent_spec/infer_transport) will also need updates.
  Suggestion: Name those test modules explicitly so the dev agent runs the full affected suite rather than the three listed files.
- [P1] [openai-gpt-5.4] The plan does not include the real config-ingestion path that must change for the new canonical YAML shape to work. src/theforge/config/load.py::_parse_models_section currently accepts models.enabled only as list[str], _parse_custom_model_registry still parses provider-like overlay tokens via overlay_transport(), and src/theforge/config/profiles.py / src/theforge/config/bridge.py still construct ModelProfile from legacy cli/provider fields. As written, the documented models.enabled: [{provider, model, transport: {kind}}] shape cannot load end-to-end.
  Suggestion: Expand the plan to explicitly cover src/theforge/config/load.py, src/theforge/config/_loaders.py, src/theforge/config/profiles.py, and src/theforge/config/bridge.py, and update derive_roles()/ModelRef plumbing to consume normalized model declarations instead of string registry keys plus legacy transport fields.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.4] Step 4 renames fallback config in types.py / schema.py / models.py, but the live fallback behavior is implemented elsewhere: src/theforge/config/profiles.py::_parse_provider_fallbacks and _apply_provider_fallback, src/theforge/config/load.py::_derive_auto_provider_fallbacks, and src/theforge/runners/cli.py::_build_api_fallback_profile. If those modules are not part of the refactor, runtime will still carry provider-named fallback state and legacy CLI→API rewrite logic after load, which breaks AC8-AC10.
  Suggestion: Add those fallback parser/application modules and the CLI fallback runner path to the plan, and make the rename a full raw-input-to-runtime migration so only normalized transport-fallback objects survive past config loading.

Step 4 renames fallback config in types.py / schema.py / models.py, but the live fallback behavior is implemented elsewhere: src/theforge/config/profiles.py::_parse_provider_fallbacks and _apply_provider_fallback, src/theforge/config/load.py::_derive_auto_provider_fallbacks, and src/theforge/runners/cli.py::_build_api_fallback_profile. If those modules are not part of the refactor, runtime will still carry provider-named fallback state and legacy CLI→API rewrite logic after load, which breaks AC8-AC10.

findings.description: AC7 requires that provider/model identity and transport identity be 'preserved distinctly in status, audit, model profile, and assignment telemetry,' but no requirement in the Summary or Desired behavior section mentions status, audit, model profile, or assignment telemetry surfaces at all — those sections only describe the config schema, loader, and dispatch resolution. This is an orphaned acceptance criterion with no corresponding requirement to anchor its scope (which fields, which surfaces, what 'distinctly' means operationally).

The story bundles two separable concerns: (a) the core model-identity schema/loader/dispatch normalization (ACs 1-6, 9-10), which is self-contained config and runtime-dispatch work, and (b) propagating that identity distinctly through status, audit, model-profile, and assignment-telemetry surfaces (AC7), which touches unrelated observability/reporting subsystems with their own data shapes and consumers. AC7's surfaces are not derivable from the identity model itself and would require separate investigation of each telemetry/audit consumer, making it a poor fit for review alongside the schema/loader change.

stories.name: Normalize model identity schema, loader, and runtime dispatch
acs: The model config schema has a first-class transport object with a bounded kind enum of cli and api.
Canonical model identity is derived from provider, model, and transport kind, with no required free-form id that can diverge from that tuple.
CLI/API selection is never encoded in provider-like prefixes in normalized config; existing keys such as openai-api/... or gemini-cli/... are removed or treated only as raw input aliases.
Runner/executor is inferred from provider plus transport kind where unambiguous; config only requires an explicit runner when the tuple has more than one valid executor.
Local LLMs are represented as API transports with endpoint metadata such as base_url; local is not a separate provider prefix or transport kind.
Routing policy (tier, capability, cost rank, dev capability, phase eligibility) is separate from and does not define model identity.
After loading, runtime dispatch reads only the normalized transport object and does not infer dispatch from legacy cli/provider field combinations.
Legacy transport fields and names are removed from runtime-facing dataclasses where practical; retained compatibility fields are confined to raw parsing/migration code.

finding_registry.description: A models config with overrides.dev.transport.kind set to api on a CLI-derived dev profile loads the dev profile as the Codex CLI transport instead of the OpenAI API transport.
The local/privacy-first provider setup guide presents the recommended configuration as profiles entries with provider: openai and no first-class transport object.

Applying an override of the canonical form overrides.dev.transport: {kind: api} to a CLI-transport profile (e.g. cli=claude) leaves the resulting ModelProfile's transport, mode, and cli fields unchanged at cli/'cli' instead of switching to the API transport, even though _resolve_override_transport correctly computed the API TransportSpec.

The same defect exists in _apply_ref_overrides: overriding a ModelRef with {'transport': {'kind': 'api'}} alone (no 'cli'/'provider' keys) computes the correct API TransportSpec in _resolve_ref_override_transport, but the constructed ModelRef still carries the old cli value, and ModelRef.__post_init__ re-derives the transport from that stale cli, discarding the intended switch.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules
Keep modules single-purpose; extract instead of growing monolith files
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Normalize model configuration around provider, model, and transport.kind, then push legacy transport spellings back to raw parsing or migration-only handling. Runtime config, dispatch, telemetry, tests, and docs should all consume the same canonical shape.

steps.description: Define the canonical runtime model/profile shape
steps.details: Keep TransportSpec as the bounded cli/api transport object, remove runtime dependence on legacy cli/provider dispatch fields, introduce an explicit routing/policy container for tier, capability, cost_rank, dev_capable, and phase_eligibility, and ensure canonical identity is derived only from provider, model, and transport.kind.

steps.description: Replace provider-prefix registry keys and overlays with canonical identities
steps.details: Remove openai-api, gemini-cli, and similar provider-like transport prefixes from normalized registry and overlay paths. If aliases are retained, confine them to raw lookup/migration input and normalize immediately to provider, model, and transport.kind. Represent local OpenAI-compatible models as api transport entries with base_url metadata.

steps.description: Make runtime dispatch read normalized transport only
steps.details: Remove dispatch inference from legacy cli/provider combinations after loading. Infer runner/executor from provider plus transport.kind where unambiguous, and require explicit runner only for genuinely ambiguous provider/transport tuples.

steps.description: Rename and normalize CLI-to-API fallback configuration
steps.details: Replace provider-family fallback naming with an explicit transport fallback concept for CLI to API. Ensure fallback entries normalize to the same provider/model/transport identity shape and do not reintroduce provider-prefix dispatch.

steps.description: Preserve distinct identity and transport fields in observability surfaces
steps.details: Audit status, assignment, model profile, and audit telemetry consumers that currently read registry_id, cli, provider, or prefixed provider tokens. Update them to emit provider, model, transport.kind, and any endpoint metadata distinctly, while keeping routing metadata separate from identity.

steps.description: Update configuration examples and migration-facing docs
steps.details: Show only the canonical provider/model/transport shape as recommended configuration. Document old provider-prefix and cli/provider spellings only as rejected or migration-only inputs if compatibility aliases are retained.

steps.description: Update tests around loading, normalization, dispatch, and migration behavior
steps.details: Adjust existing tests to assert canonical transport normalization, no runtime dispatch from legacy cli/provider combinations, local models as API transports with base_url, separated routing policy, renamed CLI-to-API fallback behavior, and telemetry/profile preservation of provider/model versus transport identity.

criteria_mapping.criterion: The model config schema has a first-class transport object with a bounded kind enum of cli and api.
Canonical model identity is derived from provider, model, and transport kind. There is no required free-form id that can diverge from that tuple.
CLI/API selection is never encoded in provider-like prefixes in normalized config. Existing keys such as openai-api/... or gemini-cli/... are removed or treated only as raw input aliases.
Runner/executor is inferred from provider plus transport kind where unambiguous; config only requires an explicit runner when the tuple has more than one valid executor.
Local LLMs are represented as API transports with endpoint metadata such as base_url; local is not a separate provider prefix or transport kind.
Routing policy is separate from identity. Tier, capability, cost rank, dev capability, and phase eligibility do not define the model identity.
Provider/model identity and transport identity are preserved distinctly in status, audit, model profile, and assignment telemetry.
Provider fallback configuration is renamed or normalized so it is clearly a transport fallback from CLI to API, not a provider-family fallback.
After loading, runtime dispatch reads only the normalized transport object. It does not infer dispatch from legacy cli/provider field combinations.

Legacy transport fields and names are removed from runtime-facing dataclasses where practical; any retained compatibility fields are confined to raw parsing/migration code and are not the source of dispatch truth.
Documentation shows only the canonical shape as the recommended configuration. Any old shape, if documented, is marked as rejected or migration-only.

risks.description: The spec permits either rejecting old spellings or retaining temporary aliases, but does not choose one.
risks.mitigation: Prefer rejection for schema integrity unless current tests or migration requirements already depend on aliases; if aliases remain, keep them strictly at raw parsing/migration boundaries.

risks.description: Telemetry and assignment consumers may be spread outside the preflight file list.
risks.mitigation: Use repository-wide searches for legacy fields and prefixed provider tokens, then update only consumers that are runtime-facing or observability-facing.

risks.description: Runner ambiguity rules are underspecified for future providers or multiple executors.
risks.mitigation: Encode only currently known unambiguous mappings and require explicit runner for any tuple with more than one executor rather than adding permissive fallback behavior.
